summary: The biggest near-term opportunity is EASD 2026 (Milan, Sep 28–Oct 2). Several press releases are already embargo-lifted on MedicalXpress, and mainstream outlets and creators haven't picked them up yet. Three are worth catching early: 1) cutting ultra-processed food and staying active offset genetic diabetes risk (UK Biobank, n=56,964); 2) 55% of newly diagnosed T2D patients hit kidney disease, heart failure or death within 10 years (n=1.6M); 3) full retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 results land Wed Sep 30. The HRT pills vs patches clot study (BMJ, Danish registry) is still our strongest rising topic. Momentum climbed across snapshots (82→86→88) and expert reactions are spreading internationally. A fresh sleep cluster is forming: CNN today covered the PNAS study where a 20-minute workout matched a 90-minute nap for memory after 30 hours awake. Australia's daylight-saving switch (Oct 4) is trending and opens a seasonal clock-change series that runs to the UK (Oct 25) and US (Nov 1) fall-back. Three topics are fading in our snapshots: FMT/IBS, the menopause proteome, and 10 diets for aging. Treat them as lower priority. Three topics need caution framing: the tirzepatide brown-fat study is mice only; the pesticide/breast-cancer paper is a chemical-database screen, not a study of people; and the Galleri and mammogram items are screening topics. Google Trends was dominated by sports today and gave no direct health signal apart from AU 'daylight savings'.

candidates.topic: Menopause HRT pills vs patches/gels and blood clots: about 1 extra serious leg/lung clot per 1,000 women per year on oral HRT; no overall increase with transdermal (The BMJ, Danish nationwide nested case-control, women 50–69)
candidates.angle: 'Same hormone, different road in': why the route (pill vs patch/gel) matters more than the dose for clot risk. Explained in absolute numbers, with a 'questions to ask your clinician' ending. Never advise switching.
candidates.why_now: Published Sep 23. Momentum has risen across 3 snapshots (82→86→88). BMJ press release, MedicalXpress, News-Medical and Science Media Centre expert reactions (AU/NZ) are all live. Menopause is a top-growth topic for women 40–55 on TikTok and Instagram, and few creators have explained the absolute risk properly yet.

evidence.signal: Contemporary menopausal hormone therapy and thrombotic disease: nationwide nested case-control study (Sep 23, 2026)
Oral HRT linked to higher leg/lung clot risk regardless of dose or duration; transdermal showed no general increase
Expert reaction round-up, Sep 24

candidates.topic: Your genes aren't your diabetes destiny: cutting ultra-processed food plus 150 min/week of activity was linked to 49% lower type 2 diabetes risk in people at high genetic risk (UK Biobank, 56,964 adults, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Bad genes, good odds': the numbers on how much diet and movement offset inherited risk. Each 10% more UPF by diet weight was linked to 7% higher risk; meeting activity guidelines was linked to 39% lower risk. Observational, so we say 'linked to'.
keywords: can you prevent diabetes if it runs in family
candidates.why_now: The EASD press release went live on MedicalXpress tonight, before the congress opens Sep 28. Mainstream coverage hasn't started, and UPF is a proven high-search evergreen topic that this refreshes. Note: average participant age was 69.5 and there were 926 cases, so on-screen text must state that scope.

evidence.signal: 56,964 UK Biobank adults, 7.8-yr follow-up; 926 cases; −39% with activity; −49% combined in high genetic risk
62nd Annual Meeting, Milan, Sep 28–Oct 2

candidates.topic: Retatrutide (triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonist) full TRIUMPH-2 results in people with type 2 diabetes, presented at EASD Wed Sep 30
candidates.angle: 'The triple-hormone shot': what a third hormone (glucagon) adds, what the full data show beyond the July topline, and what's still unknown (safety, muscle, availability). No dosing, no 'how to get it'.
candidates.why_now: The full phase 3 data are scheduled for Wednesday at EASD, and Novo also has a press briefing on Sep 30. Retatrutide already has strong search interest from the July topline (up to ~50 lb at 80 weeks). Publishing an explainer the day of release catches the spike.

evidence.signal: Full TRIUMPH-2 results to be presented Wednesday
Novo press briefing Sep 30 at EASD (Wegovy pill, amylin pipeline)

candidates.topic: 20 minutes of cycling matched a 90-minute nap for memory after 30 hours awake (PNAS, small study, healthy adults 18–35)
candidates.angle: 'Wrecked after a bad night? Nap or move?' Both improved image-memory performance by about 22% vs doing nothing, but by different brain mechanisms. Clear caveats: small young sample, extreme sleep loss, doesn't make drowsy driving safe.
keywords: how to function on no sleep
candidates.why_now: CNN published today and it was syndicated to dozens of US local stations within hours. Highly practical and a perfect Shorts hook, with thin creator coverage so far.

evidence.signal: Nap or quick workout? Published Sep 26, 2026
Original study coverage: workout or nap can help the sleepless brain (PNAS)

candidates.topic: More REM sleep linked to lower risk of 83 diseases (PLOS Medicine, 95,559 UK Biobank wearers)
candidates.angle: 'The sleep stage your tracker undersells': what REM does, what the association does and doesn't prove, and evidence-based ways to protect REM (alcohol timing, consistent wake time).
keywords: how to get more REM sleep
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3 snapshots with inc.com, ScienceDaily and KSNV coverage. Momentum is flattening (80→78→76), so publish now or skip. Pair it with the nap/workout and daylight-saving hooks for a sleep week.

evidence.signal: More REM sleep linked to lower risk of 83 diseases
Mainstream pickup Sep 25

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only ~20% of semaglutide's heart benefit (SELECT mediation analysis, European Heart Journal)
candidates.angle: 'It's not just the pounds': what else GLP-1s may be doing to arteries (inflammation, blood pressure), and why this matters for people who lose little weight. Stay strictly within what the mediation analysis estimated.
candidates.why_now: EHJ published Sep 23, plus a companion Diabetes Care SELECT paper (predictors of peak weight loss) on Sep 24. EASD week will keep GLP-1s in the news. Little creator coverage of the mediation angle so far.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide and cardiovascular risk reduction: a mediation analysis of the SELECT trial

candidates.topic: Your smartwatch may overestimate calories burned, and the error grows with body fat percentage (PLOS One, 4 watches vs metabolic cart)
candidates.angle: 'Don't eat back your watch calories': what the device actually measured (activity energy expenditure, lab conditions) and how to use trackers wisely. Keep the scope exact.
candidates.why_now: MedicalXpress coverage today. This is a relatable, shareable myth-bust with huge search volume on 'Apple Watch calories'. Mainstream hasn't picked it up yet.

evidence.signal: The higher your body fat percentage, the less accurate your smartwatch is at measuring calories burned (Sep 26)

candidates.topic: 55% of people newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes developed kidney disease, heart failure or died within 10 years (1.6M US patients, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'The decade after diagnosis': kidney disease showed up first more often than heart failure (19% vs 8.3% within 5 years). Why the kidney tests (urine albumin) are worth asking about, framed as questions for your clinician.
candidates.why_now: EASD release is live. It pairs with a JAMA paper this week on urine albumin- vs protein-creatinine ratios, and a BMJ target-trial on SGLT2/GLP-1 kidney outcomes. Low creator coverage. Outcome is a combined endpoint (CKD, HF or death) and must be stated exactly.

evidence.signal: Combined risk 33% at 5 yrs, 55% at 10 yrs; n=1,617,508

candidates.topic: That 'fresh clean' smell: scented cleaners + indoor ozone create large numbers of nanoparticles within minutes (Purdue, ACS Fall 2026)
candidates.angle: 'What you're actually breathing after you clean': the chemistry (terpenes + ozone), what's known vs unknown about health effects, and simple, evidence-based ventilation tips. No fear-mongering.

evidence.signal: That fresh cleaning smell could be filling your home with nanoparticles (Sep 26)
